title: Human Capability Constitution bound into universal Naya boot
nutshell: Words were converted into a canonical operating standard, bound into the universal boot path, and recorded in the current-state feed. Full behavioral enforcement remains unproven.
human: Words have low value without action; NayaNET must prove understanding by changing the system.
child: If we say the system should make people more capable, we must build and test behavior that actually helps people understand, decide, act, remember, and improve.
grandma: A promise becomes useful when it changes how the house works for the next person.
naya: Created the canonical Human Capability Constitution, bound it into the universal boot directive, updated current state, and preserved an explicit enforcement gap instead of claiming completion.
weaver: A principle becomes materially real when it changes the canonical execution path and leaves an auditable receipt. The next step is executable enforcement, not more prose.
lesson: DOCUMENTED is not IMPLEMENTED; IMPLEMENTED is not VERIFIED; and policy text is not behavioral proof.
meaning: The Constitution is now canonical and boot-bound. Its full effect remains an explicit engineering task.
next_action: Build machine-readable Human Capability criteria, a validator/test, and an end-to-end proof that a consequential human action creates durable retrievable intelligence that improves a subsequent interaction.
